goal: Arduino Uno with a common-cathode RGB LED: red leg on D9, green on D10, blue on D11, each through a 220 ohm resistor, common leg to GND. It fades smoothly through the rainbow.

plan.title: RGB LED Rainbow Mood Light
plan.summary: Build a smooth rainbow fader using a common-cathode RGB LED connected to an Arduino Uno. Three PWM pins control the red, green, and blue colour channels through current-limiting resistors, creating seamless colour transitions across the entire spectrum.
plan.final_result: When powered via USB, the RGB LED cycles continuously through all colors of the rainbow (red to yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, and back to red) with smooth, flicker-free fading.
safety: Always disconnect the USB cable before placing or moving any wires or parts on the breadboard.
Ensure each LED anode leg passes through its own 220 ohm resistor; connecting any anode directly to 5V will burn out the LED.
Verify the longest leg is in row 21 and grounded so that reverse voltage does not damage the diode elements.

parts.why: Provides power and runs the firmware code that generates PWM signals to fade each colour channel.

parts.name: Breadboard, full size (830 tie points)
parts.why: Holds the LED, resistors, and jumper wires together securely without soldering.

parts.name: RGB LED 5 mm (common cathode)
parts.why: Combines red, green, and blue diodes into a single bulb sharing a common ground leg.

parts.name: 220 ohm resistor

parts.name: Jumper wires
parts.why: Carries ground and control signals between the Arduino Uno and breadboard rows.

part_guide.breadboard: A white plastic prototyping grid with internal metal clips that let you plug in electronic components without soldering.
part_guide.arduino: An Arduino Uno microcontroller board with blue solder mask that runs your sketch and provides controllable 5V PWM power.
part_guide.rgb_led: A 5 mm diffused round LED with 4 legs. The second leg from the left is the longest (common cathode ground), flanked by red, green, and blue anode legs.
part_guide.resistor_red: A small beige cylinder with red, red, brown, and gold color bands. It limits current specifically into the red anode pin.
part_guide.resistor_green: A small beige cylinder with red, red, brown, and gold color bands. It limits current specifically into the green anode pin.
part_guide.resistor_blue: A small beige cylinder with red, red, brown, and gold color bands. It limits current specifically into the blue anode pin.
part_guide.wire_gnd_rail: A black jumper wire that connects the Arduino Uno GND pin to the outer ground rail line along the top edge of the breadboard.
part_guide.wire_cathode: A black jumper wire that links the common cathode row (row 21) directly up to the top ground rail.
part_guide.wire_red: A red jumper wire that feeds PWM pin D9 pulses to row 16 for the red colour channel.
part_guide.wire_green: A green jumper wire that feeds PWM pin D10 pulses to row 26 for the green colour channel.
part_guide.wire_blue: A blue jumper wire that feeds PWM pin D11 pulses to row 27 for the blue colour channel.

steps.title: Insert the RGB LED
steps.instruction: Take the 4-pin RGB LED and find the longest leg (the common cathode). Insert the red anode leg into row 20, column e (left of the centre gap), the longest cathode leg into row 21, column e, the green anode leg into row 22, column e, and the blue anode leg into row 23, column e.
steps.check: The RGB LED stands upright spanning four consecutive holes in column e, from row 20 down to row 23, with its longest lead firmly seated in e21.

steps.title: Place the Red Channel Resistor
steps.instruction: Take a 220 ohm resistor (red, red, brown color bands). Bend both legs 90 degrees downward and push one leg into row 16, column d (left of the centre gap) and the other leg into row 20, column d (sharing row 20 with the red LED leg).
steps.check: A 220 ohm resistor bridges rows 16 and 20 in column d, sharing row 20 with the red pin of the LED.
